requirements.requirement: Create/ensure account `datauser` and target directory `/srv/data` on node1
requirements.summary: cmd-e7d9f13f6725417e shows datauser absent and /srv/data absent at baseline. cmd-539b6db755e04500 creates datauser via useradd and creates /srv/data owned by datauser:datauser mode 750, confirmed by ls -ld output. Re-verified present in cmd-09f227b8abfc4e97.

requirements.requirement: Limit datauser to 100 MB of storage under /srv/data, enforced by the filesystem itself (not an application-level check)
requirements.summary: Root XFS filesystem was mounted noquota at baseline (cmd-e7d9f13f6725417e). Executor set rootflags=pquota via grubby and added pquota to /etc/fstab (cmd-539b6db755e04500), rebooted the node to apply it, and after reboot confirmed the root fs remounted with prjquota (cmd-09f227b8abfc4e97). XFS project 100 was mapped to /srv/data via /etc/projects and /etc/projid and named 'datauser', and a 100M hard block limit was set with `xfs_quota limit -p bhard=100m`. Enforcement was directly demonstrated: a 50MB write by datauser succeeded, and a subsequent 80MB write was rejected by the kernel with ENOSPC once usage reached exactly 100M ('dd: error writing ... No space left on device', 50+0 records written before failure), and the quota report confirmed Used=100M/Hard=100M. This is a genuine kernel/filesystem-level enforcement mechanism (XFS project quotas), not an application check.

requirements.requirement: Node1 restart evidence protocol: pre-restart boot identity/health, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id 5fb1b173-... was captured in cmd-539b6db755e04500, matching the fixed global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity snapshot. `systemctl reboot` was issued non-interactively in cmd-74019cb33b974e71 with the exec stream closing as expected during shutdown. A first poll timed out while the node was offline (cmd-50f0982bd6ab4b17, expected transient state), and a second poll (cmd-bd27731e3bd644f3) returned a new boot_id 22bbbbcb-..., matching the fixed global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity snapshot and diverging from baseline in the executor_comparison diff. Post-restart, sshd was confirmed active, the root filesystem was healthy and remounted with prjquota, and the quota configuration/test performed and cleaned up after the restart, all in cmd-09f227b8abfc4e97 and cmd-6db2e3209e644f75, which also re-confirms the boot_id and shows quota usage reset to 0 after test-file cleanup.

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the task: datauser and /srv/data were created, XFS project quota (persistently enabled via grubby rootflags=pquota and fstab, requiring and validated by a reboot) was configured to cap datauser at 100MB under /srv/data, and kernel-level enforcement was directly proven with a passing 50MB write followed by an ENOSPC failure on an 80MB write at exactly 100M used. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also cleanly executed with a verified boot-identity change and recovered post-restart health, and all temporary test artifacts were cleaned up with quota usage restored to 0.
limitations: Persistence of the specific xfs_quota project limit across a further future reboot was not directly re-tested (only the pquota mount option's persistence was validated via the single executed reboot); this is inferred from standard XFS on-disk quota metadata behavior rather than directly observed a second time.
The cluster/topology contains only node1, so no multi-node cluster-state recovery could be observed beyond the single node's own health checks.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every state-changing command has a clear causal link to the task or the mandatory restart protocol: user/directory creation, grubby/fstab edits for pquota, the reboot itself, project-quota configuration and limit-setting, and the bounded 50MB/80MB test writes used to prove kernel enforcement. The test files (small.bin, big.bin) were fully removed in cmd-6db2e3209e644f75, with quota usage confirmed back to 0/100M and the executor-comparison diff showing no residual filesystem changes beyond the expected boot-identity and post-reboot listening-socket/PID churn. No unnecessary, unreverted, or unrelated mutations were found; no failed services were introduced (failed-services observation stayed empty before and after); package-health manager reporting was unaffected.
